title: Under the Hood: Off-Heap ProcBin Refc Binaries & Avoiding Sub-Binary Leaks (binary:copy/1)
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates sub-binary unpinning via binary:copy/1 and memory diagnostic inspection using binary:referenced_byte_size/1.

typesSpec: Returns independent standalone copy of Subject
otpDocCards.description: Creates a standalone heap copy of a binary or sub-binary, severing off-heap buffer references.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(N) copy, frees large pinned refc binary buffers.

otpDocCards.description: Returns the size in bytes of the underlying off-heap binary buffer referenced by Subject.

mentalModelCheck.question: When pattern matching <<Header:16/binary, _Rest/binary>> from a 64 MB video packet, why does calling binary:copy(Header) resolve the memory leak?

options.label: binary:copy/1 forces the 16 bytes into a fresh Heap Binary (< 64 bytes), allowing the 64 MB ProcBin reference count to drop to 0 and get freed
options.explanation: By copying the 16-byte slice, you allocate a private heap binary. The original 64 MB off-heap ProcBin no longer has any references pinning it, allowing immediate GC reclamation.

options.label: binary:copy/1 compresses the binary using gzip
options.explanation: binary:copy/1 performs term cloning to unpin off-heap buffers, not compression.

options.label: binary:copy/1 moves the binary to an ETS table
options.explanation: binary:copy/1 produces a normal Erlang binary on the calling process heap.
